svg.title: One number hides the slice where it fails
svg.desc: A staircase of baseline scores climbing from random 0.4997 through one feature 0.8014 to the model 0.8991, beside a confident overall accuracy bar cracking into a strong self-serve slice at 0.9548 and a weak enterprise slice at 0.5842 whose boxes are redrawn proportional to revenue rather than row count, giving a revenue-weighted 0.8457, plus two bootstrap confidence intervals drawn against a heavy zero line and a three-box offline-shadow-online chain with two boxes still empty.
svg.text: One number hides the slice where it fails
the ladder you have to climb
if you cannot beat ONE FEATURE,
stop and go back to the data.
now drawn to scale by REVENUE, not by row count
the model is a coin flip
is the new model actually better? bootstrap, 2000 resamples
both clear of zero, one of them barely
the three numbers, and only one of them exists yet
MEASUREMENT you plan for, not a surprise
...and then? -> shadow it for a week before anyone believes it
